parallel.requirements: Recognized the required installable GraphNeuralNetwork package, including GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, load_data_v1/preprocess_adj, examples, tests, setup.py, and unified API exports.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept an end-to-end plan but spawned sparse/runtime and test-shape child branches; those branches also acted as implementation owners rather than pure advisors.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote package metadata, data utilities, models, training helpers, examples, bundled sample Cora data, and tests; child branches independently wrote overlapping implementations and probes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final tree came from the shared workspace after parent-side fixes, but multiple live agents touched the same package files and children were interrupted before final parent-visible handoff.
parallel.verification: Parallel parent ran py_compile/import checks, pytest until 14 passed, setup.py verify, and attempted an example smoke that exposed missing run exports before closing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 0 of 4; no submit command was invoked, child branches were interrupted, and visible example-run API smoke failure was not fully resolved before final response.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same complete package obligations, including model classes/layers, data preprocessing, training helpers, examples, tests, setup.py dependencies, and public API exports.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned scaffolding, implementation, tests, packaging, verification, cleanup, and final response without delegation or concurrent ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: Serial created README/license/setup, gnn utilities, GCN/GAT/GraphSAGE modules, example runners, tests, fallback/Cora loaders, and checkpointed training support in one timeline.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial assembled one coherent final workspace, installed it editable, confirmed a checkpoint file, and listed final files without multi-agent merge or collision steps.
serial.verification: Serial ran compileall, pytest to 10 passed, editable install, and a one-epoch checkpointed GCN training path, then noted no submit command was available.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 0 of 4 despite local verification; likely hidden tests required behavior beyond the local suite, and no actual submit interface was used by the agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the complete GNN package requirements and reported implementing models, utilities, examples, tests, and setup metadata.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt and reported implementing the same core package surface and training utilities.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition gap is proven; both failed official tests despite claiming broad coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent spawned probe/check children but retained its own implementation plan; children also independently implemented overlapping files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor and one todo plan to own the whole pipeline from scaffolding through verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping active ownership of the same package surface, while serial had single-owner sequencing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs are encrypted, but visible behavior shows children treated the task as implementation work and then encountered shared workspace mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept context within one actor and did not need child handoffs or cross-agent file/interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced opaque delegation and implicit shared-workspace interfaces; serial avoided those transfer boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote package modules, utilities, training helpers, data files, and tests, then patched API and test issues after failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same broad package surface sequentially and made smaller follow-up fixes around dropout/training behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented similar broad functionality, but parallel's path included concurrent overlapping file creation and reconciliation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited on children, saw them still running, interrupted direct child branches, and closed with no direct child final handoff integrated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and proceeded from local commands to final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only parallel had a child lifecycle failure: explicit cancellation before direct child results reached the parent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent and children wrote overlapping source/config/test files in the same apparent workspace and had to react to unexpected file state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial file writes occurred in one actor timeline, with no subagent writes, merge collisions, or overlapping file ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had direct same-file shared-state collisions; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel passed local pytest and setup verification but also observed an example-run import failure and still lacked a submit command.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed local pytest, editable install, and checkpointed training, then also lacked a submit command.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accepted local verification rather than official submit; parallel added a visible failed smoke of example run exports before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, many more LLM/tool calls, waited on children, interrupted them, and closed after about 662 agent seconds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer calls, finished in about 483 agent seconds, and closed after local verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra budget on child branches and collision recovery, while serial was shorter and single-threaded; both nevertheless failed official evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed status records show both parallel and serial failed all four official tests, so there is no discordant outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: the serial run built and verified a single coherent package path, while the parallel run spawned children that independently wrote overlapping package files, later had active child branches interrupted, and still closed on local verification rather than official submit. These parallel coordination problems created rework and lost child work, but they do not explain a pass/fail split because both attempts failed 0/4.
parallel_contributors: Overlapping child and parent writes caused same-file reconciliation and extra local debugging before finalization.
Direct child branches were interrupted while still running, preventing final parent-visible handoffs.
The parent relied on local pytest/setup checks and could not invoke a real submit command.
serial_contributors: Single actor implementation avoided child lifecycle and shared-file coordination hazards.
Serial also relied on local pytest/install/training checks and could not invoke a real submit command.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial created fewer local tests and omitted some files present in the parallel artifact, while parallel created extra tests and duplicated bundled package data.
Parallel saw a failed example runner import of a non-existent run function but did not convert that smoke failure into an API fix before final response.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are supported parallel adverse process effects, not an exclusive official-failure root cause

candidates.reason: The parent and child branches all treated themselves as implementation owners; the problem was overlapping ownership, not absence of an implementer.
The parent acted as integrator by reading files, patching API mismatches, running tests, and finalizing the workspace; integration was not ownerless.
The parent owned final package placement and final response; no required build or deliverable placement was left without an assigned owner.
The parent maintained an end-to-end plan covering scaffolding, implementation, tests, verification, and closure, even though coordination was flawed.
The parent did not block productive implementation behind one mandatory serial preflight; it wrote package files while probes were running.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation as a separate first phase before implementation; implementation proceeded concurrently with probes.
No indispensable implementation path was merely starved while auxiliary workers consumed capacity; direct write collision and child termination explain the adverse events more specifically.
Although the parallel run used many tokens and several children, it did not time out and the retained events are direct collision and cancellation boundaries, not collective budget exhaustion.
A child branch expanded into broad implementation, but the delegation payload is encrypted and the observed adverse chain is better captured by same-file collision and explicit interruption.
The child briefs are encrypted, and the visible record does not prove an already-known requirement was omitted from a child delegation and then followed to failure.
The retained problem is live agents editing the same source paths, not separately owned components that merely lacked an interface contract.
There is no proved known finding that disappeared through a summary or transfer before a receiver repeated work; the child results mostly never reached the parent.
No returned handoff containing needed information was too large for the parent to reduce; the issue was absent/terminated handoff, not bulky consumption.
No receiver acted on a handoff describing a superseded workspace state; observed stale-looking file assumptions came from concurrent writes, classified under same-file collision.
The record does not show incompatible returned reports left unadjudicated; conflicts appeared as on-disk file/API mismatches rather than handoff reports.

The parent did close after local checks despite official failure, but no non-evaluator evidence proves a parent-visible required integrated acceptance gap caused by coordination rather than ordinary verification limits.
No replacement or retry agent was launched without inherited findings and shown to repeat prior work; the extra child activity was concurrent, not a retry episode.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent observed delegated children still running and explicitly interrupted both direct child branches before either direct branch returned a final result to the parent.
candidates.realized_consequence: The delegated probe branches did not deliver final parent-visible handoffs, and in-progress child work was lost when the parent closed from its own local checks.
candidates.near_match_reason: The waits are part of the story, but the decisive lifecycle event is explicit interruption after status inspection rather than passive waiting without inspection.

candidates.reason: There was no complete unpromoted candidate left merely because final packaging started too late; the parent produced a final tree and the child work was interrupted/unjoined.
No child implementation was merged after the relevant integrated verification without a later check; the parent's final checks occurred after its own edits.
No completed direct child implementation was returned and available for parent adoption; the closest lifecycle defect is explicit interruption before final handoff.
A nested sparse probe produced useful findings, but the direct parent-visible lifecycle was the parent interrupting the still-running child branch before it returned.
The retained lifecycle event is cancellation of active children; the parent did continue its own implementation path rather than leaving a failed child as the sole owner.
No completed direct child result was available to the parent and then ignored; the children were still running when the parent interrupted them.
The parent did wait and time out, but it also inspected agent status and then explicitly interrupted the children, so Early Child Termination is the direct boundary.
The write conflict involved the same package files, so Same-File Collision is the more specific concurrent-write label.

The parent and child branches independently wrote overlapping package source, config, and test files while live, and child branches then encountered unexpected on-disk contents and patch/import mismatches.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel workspace incurred reconciliation and retest work from unexpected shared file state, including failed patch assumptions and import/API mismatches before finalization.
candidates.near_match_reason: The record shows same-file live edits and reconciliation, but not one directly proven wholesale source replacement by a specific actor.

candidates.reason: The record proves same-file concurrent edits and reconciliation, but not a single directly proven wholesale replacement of another agent's non-entry source file.
The evidence does not prove replacement of the directly submitted entry point or executable deliverable while another agent owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current final outputs and invalidated another agent's final-tree provenance.
Shared workspace writing occurred, but Same-File Collision is more specific because overlapping same source paths and reconciliation are directly evidenced.
No generated cache, fixture, temporary path, or auxiliary artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable input or reference environment.
